title: 2003 HMMT February Guts Problem 32
statement: If \(x, y\), and \(z\) are real numbers such that \(2 x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=2 x-4 y+2 x z-5\), find the maximum possible value of \(x-y+z\).

solutions.text:
4
The equation rearranges as \((x-1)^{2}+(y+2)^{2}+(x-z)^{2}=0\), so we must have \(x=1\), \(y=-2, z=1\), giving us 4 .
